text:
kevin: noticed a strange spike in org-level quota consumption last night. looks like a bunch of requests routed off project keys to an org SA during a throttling window. support tickets inbound.
nora: can you share a sample trace or headers?
kevin: minimal proxy log:
```
POST /v1/chat
Authorization: Bearer key-proj-77
X-Project: proj-77
```
proxy decided to route to `org-sa:billing-pool` at runtime due to per-project throttles. billing export shows charge to proj-77 but internal quota table lists `owner=org-sa:billing-pool` so dashboards are inconsistent.
eli: two separate concerns: billing attribution (what customer pays) vs quota ownership (what bucket is decremented). currently we use incoming headers for billing, runtime principal for quota. that mismatch will confuse both customers and SRE.
sam: options: 1) derive both billing and quota from declared project header (keep current billing behavior), 2) derive both from effective principal (post-routing), or 3) emit both dimensions and keep dashboards explicit.
product-ops: option 3 sounds safest for now. expose both declared_owner and effective_owner in UI, mark rows where they differ. that helps support and billing reconcile without flipping semantics.
kevin: agree, but we need quick telemetry to investigate historical impact. propose adding a single event `auth.routing.attribution` emitted at decision time with fields: declared_owner, effective_owner, routing_reason, request_id.
eli: add sampling and a schema version. sample payload (text only):
```
event: auth.routing.attribution
declared_owner: proj-77
effective_owner: org-sa:billing-pool
routing_reason: project_quota_throttle
schema_version: v1
```
qa-bot: alert created: monitor "attribution-delta-rate" when >1% sustained for 30m.
nora: UX: quota page should show a small badge "routed" with hover containing routing_reason and a link to traces. also a bulk filter: show only routed requests in last 24h.
eli: implementation note: compute effective_owner after the routing policy module finalizes, then emit the event. need to be careful about ordering so we don't double-count metrics.
sam: rollout plan: canary 2% with sampling=100% for the event for 48h, then 20% for 72h, then default sampling 10% at 100%. feature-flag `emit_routing_attribution_event` to toggle.
kevin: also add a short-term shim: when effective_owner != declared_owner, set a `routed=true` tag on the quota metric so dashboards can immediately filter.
product-ops: we should message support and billing teams before changing billing attribution. even if we don't change billing, they need the routed view.
eli: about billing: if we later change to post-routing billing, we'll need a migration window and metric `attribution_schema=v2` so historical queries remain stable. prefer to avoid changing billing without long notice.
nora: will draft a console mock and send to design. simple pill and link should be enough.
qa-bot: canary deployment scheduled: auth-proxy v2.16.0 -> 2% at 2024-10-25T02:12:00Z
sam: I'll add the feature flag and guard in the policy engine. also add a fallback: if computed effective_owner is empty, keep declared_owner to avoid orphaned metrics.
kevin: thanks. opening GH issue #4992 with telemetry schema, rollout steps, and console tickets. tagging @billing and @support.
product-ops: thanks, let's sync after the 48h snapshot.
